body:
> Designed with the operator on 2026-09-01, immediately after running track #191 (six cards, five children) and
> losing two children's work to the branch strategy the design currently prescribes.

## Why

**hkb has no concept of a track branch.** Grep `src/track.js` for one: `<base>` is only ever "the branch of the
node this one is blocked by" or "the default branch". Nothing creates an integration branch, nothing records
one, nothing merges one. The per-node brief says:

```
402:  `<base>` = the branch of the node this one is blocked by (`kb/<blocker>`), or the default branch
453:  Do the work on a branch of its own: `git switch -c kb/<n> <base>`
455:  Push and open a draft PR whose body contains `Closes #<n>`, based on that same `<base>`
```

So children chain off each other, and today that produced three distinct failures in one track:

1. **The brief has no answer for a diamond.** `<base>` is singular; #227 was blocked by **two** children, so the
   runner improvised an integration branch (`kb/191-wave1`) with nothing in the design behind it, and nothing on
   the board recording that it existed or had to reach `main`.
2. **A stacked PR is invisible to hkb.** GitHub honours `Closes #N` only for a PR targeting the default branch,
   so #227's PR was never linked, `finish` saw no PR, and the card closed as *done* with the work unmerged.
   (#234 has since landed the head-branch fallback that makes this survivable — it is why this card is now
   possible at all.)
3. **Eager merging pulls the base out from under the chain.** The root's own report put it best: *"#229's base
   branch was squash-merged and deleted mid-task… Stacked node PRs and eager merging of the lower nodes do not
   compose without either rebasing or accepting a new head branch."* Both #229 and the root ended up on
   improvised `-rebased` / `-root` heads.

The correlation is the clearest evidence: **both children with no blockers (#225, #226) sailed through; both
children with blockers (#227, #228) were lost. The only dependent child that worked (#229) is the one whose
subagent ignored the brief and rebased onto `main`.**

There is also a cost the current design pays every time: a child branched from `main` watches `main` move under
it as unrelated cards merge. #161 was sent back **twice** today purely to catch up — two full worker sessions
for zero content.

## What

The model, as the operator described it:

```
main
 └── kb/track-<root>            created when the track is claimed, from the default branch
      ├── kb/<child-a>          branched from the track branch, PR into it
      └── kb/<child-b>          branched from the track branch, PR into it
 └── kb/track-<root> ──────────> one PR into main, after the root's own pass
```

- **The track branch is created at claim time**, from the default branch, and **recorded on the root's attempt
  row** (`track_branch`) so the board can see it. A runner that dies must not strand work nothing can find —
  that is the whole reason it goes on the row rather than living only in the runner's head.
- **Every child branches from the track branch, not from a sibling.** The diamond disappears: two blockers and
  one blocker produce the same base. Children see their blockers' merged work because the track branch has it.
- **Every child's PR targets the track branch**, is reviewed at its own scope, and merges into it. This is the
  rung that **requires #234**: none of those PRs is linkable by `closedByPullRequestsReferences`, so the
  head-branch fallback is what keeps the cards attached to them. Do not build this without it.
- **The root's pass runs on the track branch**, which already holds the assembled feature, and opens **one PR
  into `main`**. That makes the root's "check the pieces fit" verification happen *before* anything lands
  rather than after — today the root verifies work that has already shipped.
- **A stable base.** A child's base moves only when a sibling merges — the wave boundary — instead of every
  time an unrelated card lands on `main`.

### Review granularity (settled with the operator; record it, do not re-derive it)

- Each child PR is reviewed at its own scope: does this slice work, and can it be integrated into the parent.
- **The root is reviewed like any other task, because it is one.** Its PR into `main` is not a formality — it
  carries the synthesize pass and whatever docs no child could write.
- **Two children conflicting on the way into the track branch is the trigger** for reviewing the assembled
  whole. That is a detectable event, not a judgement call: the same `mergeable` / `mergeStateStatus` signal,
  observed on the track branch instead of `main`. Cheap in the common case, thorough exactly when it is not.

### What has to be decided while building

- **Lifecycle.** Who deletes the track branch, and when. What happens to it if the track is abandoned, or if the
  root is archived. An orphaned track branch is the same class of bug as an orphaned PR.
- **A dead runner.** The ordinary dispatcher must still be able to finish the graph node-by-node — that promise
  is in `DEFAULT_PROFILES`' description of `claude-track`. Decide whether it finishes them onto the track branch
  or falls back to `main`, and make `hkb doctor` able to see a track branch with no live runner.
- **`merge.mode`.** Merging a child into a track branch is a lower-stakes act than merging into `main`. Decide
  whether `operator` gates both or only the final one.

## Done when

- [ ] Claiming a track creates `kb/track-<root>` from the default branch and records it on the root's attempt row.
- [ ] Every child of a track branches from the track branch and opens its PR into it, whatever its blockers.
- [ ] A child's PR is associated with its card through the head-branch fallback, with a test using a track-branch
      base — the shape that lost #227.
- [ ] The root's pass runs on the track branch and opens one PR into the default branch.
- [ ] A conflict between two children merging into the track branch is surfaced as an event, not discovered by a
      human.
- [ ] The track branch's lifecycle is defined, and `hkb doctor` flags one with no live runner.
- [ ] `src/track.js`'s per-node brief no longer says "the branch of the node this one is blocked by".
- [ ] `npm run lint && npm test` pass; `docs/wiki/features/tracks.md` describes the model and the review rule.
goal: Claiming a track creates kb/track-<root> from the default branch and records it on the root's attempt row; every child branches from it and PRs into it whatever its blockers; the root's pass runs on it and opens one PR to main; a child-vs-child conflict is surfaced as an event; the track branch's lifecycle is defined and doctor flags one with no live runner
title: A track has no branch: children chain off each other, so a diamond has no base, a stacked PR is invisible, and eager merging pulls the base out from under the chain
